text: Track 5.1 Is it a good thing that football is such a big business these days? I'm talking to Obi Kanu, who has just signed a contract with Westchester United. Congratulations, Obi! Thank you. Let's start with Victor, the club manager of Westchester United. Victor, you've been a club manager for 30 years. Do you think that there is too much money in football? Well, yes and no. People are happy to spend lots of money on what they love. In my opinion, if there is a lot of money in football, it's because of the fans. And this is great because clubs can pay for players to have the best training, so they have more skills and get better and better. Today's players are the best ever. Okay, so football players these days are very good, but the salaries they earn are still too much. And the cost of tickets is too high. Clubs charge so much money that many fans can't afford to come to matches. Okay, but fans can still watch the game on television. A lot of money comes from television and advertising. Clubs need that money very much. The clubs often have money problems, and the club managers worry about this more than anybody else. We always have to make more money so we can attract champion players who will score goals and help us win matches. Without those players, clubs cannot continue. So, Obi, you trained at the famous Abigen football academy in Ivory Coast. What's your opinion of football as a business? Well, Ivory Coast is not a rich country. I spent all my time as a kid kicking a football around with my friends in the street. We all dreamed of getting into the academy. It's the one big chance to make money. We had to compete with each other all the time. The big prize is getting into a professional team. Then you can support your family and give them a better life. But you have to work hard and be strong. You also have to be lucky to get the opportunity. The football business is hardest to vol for the players. Clubs are businesses that buy and sell us. If you get hurt and can't play anymore, you can lose your job. Nobody cares about you after that.
